description:
## Problem Statement
Today the processor-health endpoint reports a single global value per processor. Merchants cannot distinguish their own scope.

## Solution
Extend the processor-health response with an optional merchantId scope.

## User Stories
1. As a merchant ops user, I want to query processor health for my own merchant.
2. As a merchant support agent, I want a DEGRADED status with reason codes.
3. As a merchant support agent, I want the merchant-scoped DEGRADED status visible on the internal status page.

## Cross-Application Impact
- payment-platform: extend ProcessorHealthClient with merchant-scoped lookup, add DEGRADED enum + reason-code list, plumb scope through the existing health cache.

## Implementation Decisions
- New optional `merchantId` parameter; default behavior unchanged.
- Reason-code enum lives alongside the existing health enum (additive).
- Cache key extended to `(processor, merchantId)` with inherited TTL.
- No schema changes; merchant scope is computed on-the-fly.

## Out of Scope
- walletapi changes
- customer-facing checkout error surfacing
- frontend display of reason codes
- historical reason-code analytics

## Further Notes
Coordinate with the merchant-support team on which reason codes are user-visible.

## References
- graphify nodes: ProcessorHealthClient, processor-health-cache
